18.10.0.en: 11 Terrors shall make him afraid on every side, and frighten him at his feet. 12 His strength shall be hungerbitten, and destruction shall be ready at his side. 13 He eats the members of his body. The firstborn of death eats his members.

18.10.1.en: "Terrors shall make him afraid on every side, and frighten him at his feet" [11].

18.10.2.en: He speaks here of the very ruin reserved for the wicked in the world to come, which in some form befalls them in this world. The first of this ruin is what comes upon his heart of terrors that shake his whole being, reaching down to his feet, which cannot bear him. These terrors, which arise from his sense of guilt, are a foretaste of the terrors he will suffer after his death.

18.10.3.en: Everything around him terrifies him, so that it is said of him, "The wicked flee when no man pursueth" (Prov 28:1), because what pursues him is not what is around him but what is within him.

18.10.4.en: "There is no peace, saith the LORD, unto the wicked" (Isa 48:22).

18.10.5.en: "The way of peace they know not; and there is no judgment in their goings: they have made them crooked paths: whosoever goeth therein shall not know peace" (Isa 59:8).

18.10.6.en: "They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace" (Jer 6:14; 8:11).

18.10.7.en: "We looked for peace, but no good came; and for a time of health, and behold terror!" (Jer 8:15).

18.10.8.en: "Because, even because they have seduced my people, saying, Peace; and there was no peace; and one built up a wall, and, lo, others daubed it with untempered morter" (Ezek 13:10).

18.10.9.en: "To wit, the prophets of Israel which prophesy concerning Jerusalem, and which see visions of peace for her, and there is no peace, saith the Lord GOD" (Ezek 13:16).

18.10.10.en: * And now those who do not keep the feast... these are heading toward days of sorrow, not happiness, for "there is no peace, saith the LORD, unto the wicked" (Isa 48:22). And as Wisdom says, joy and gladness are taken from their mouth. Such are the joys of the wicked.

18.10.11.en: * For what does the feast mean but the service of the soul?! And what is this service but constant prayer to God and continual thanksgiving?! So the ungrateful, who are far from this, are truly deprived of the joy that flows from it, for joy and gladness are taken from their mouths, and therefore the (divine) Word does not allow them to be at peace, for there is no peace for the wicked, saith the Lord (Isa 48:22), but they work in pain and sorrow.

18.10.12.en: St. Athanasius the Apostolic * ["Terrors make him afraid on every side"], for he imagines that all men are turned against him in this way, and so he struggles with all.

18.11.0.en: "His strength shall be hungerbitten, and destruction shall be ready at his side" [12].

18.11.1.en: The wicked man does not feel satisfied, for what he thinks is the source of his satisfaction, whether his wealth or honor or power, etc., shames him and brings him into a sense of emptiness. Beside this inner famine, ruin comes upon the wicked man, drawing near to take control of him. "They are brought into desolation, as in a moment" (Ps 73:19).

18.11.2.en: The text in the writings of Pope Gregory (the Great) reads: "Let his strength be stricken with hunger, and let famine invade his ribs" [12]...

18.11.3.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that man, being composed of soul and body, has the soul representing the strong element, while the body represents the weak element. So the wicked man, since he gives leadership to the body and its lusts, however strong he may seem, is weak, losing his inner strength and his inner satisfaction, and lives in weakness, famine and emptiness. But the spiritual man, since he gives leadership to the soul sanctified by the Spirit of God, lives in a spirit of strength and inner satisfaction, lacking nothing.

18.11.4.en: * Every man, being composed of soul and body, is as though made of strength and weakness. For by virtue of that element by which he was created a rational spirit, he is not unfittingly called strong, but with regard to the element belonging to his bodily being, he is weak. So man's strength is in his rational soul, able to resist the tendencies of evil that face him. So it is also said by the blessed Job: ["I strengthened him for a time, that he may pass away forever"] (Job 14:20), where man withdraws with his rational soul to live eternally. So the strength of this wicked man is smitten with hunger, since his soul is not fed by any inward food that refreshes it. God says of this hunger through the prophet: ["I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD"] (see Amos 8:11).

18.11.5.en: It is well added: ["Famine invades his ribs"]... Everyone's ribs are the senses of his mind which swim about his hidden thoughts. So famine invades his ribs when all spiritual food is taken away, and the senses of the mind weaken, and cannot control their thoughts or protect them.

18.11.7.en: * Someone may think that the people of Israel are rich, for they have the adoption as sons, and the divine service, and the promises and the fathers. At any rate, they became poor because of their sins against the Lord. "But they that seek the LORD shall not want any good thing" (Ps 34:10). They came to be in need of food in a certain sense, and suffer hunger. For since they killed the Bread of life, hunger for bread came upon them... they were in need and hungry.

18.11.8.en: St. Basil the Great * When Joseph was about thirty years old, he was freed from his bonds and interpreted Pharaoh's dream. He became ruler of Egypt. And in the time of plenty he gathered wheat so as to distribute it in the time of famine. I believe that Joseph's thirty years came beforehand as a type of the Savior's thirty years. For this second Joseph did not gather wheat of the same kind that the first Joseph gathered in Egypt. Jesus gathers the wheat and distributes it when famine comes upon Egypt, ["not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD"] (Amos 8:11).

18.11.9.en: Origen "He eats the members of his body."

18.12.0.en: "The firstborn of death eats his members" [13].

18.12.1.en: Death draws near to the wicked man and eats the members of his body, that is, brings him into corruption. But for the righteous, death prepares eternal glory, where the body shares in the glories of the soul.

18.12.2.en: The text in the writings of Pope Gregory (the Great) reads: "May it remove the beauty of his skin, and may the firstborn of death scatter his arms." What is the beauty of his body but temporal glory, which is eaten and passes away, for it is beauty on an outer skin, with no place in the inner depths? But of the righteous it was said: ["The king's daughter is all glorious within"] (Ps 45:13). And it was said in Zechariah the prophet: "And will be the glory in the midst of her" (Zech 2:5).

18.12.3.en: Moreover the matter does not stop at the passing of temporal glory, but death comes upon the human soul, as it withdraws from God, the source of its life and resurrection. Spiritual death kills the soul's arms, that is, makes it unable to work!

18.12.4.en: * "The beauty of his skin" is the temporary glory which he desires as something external to us, and which remains as beauty on the skin...

18.12.5.en: And what is death but sin that kills the soul in its inner life? Therefore it is written: ["Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the first resurrection"] (Rev 20:6). By this resurrection a person afterward enjoys a joyful resurrection in the body, he who, while in this life, rises again from the death of his soul...

18.12.7.en: * ["The king's daughter is all glorious within"] (Ps 45:13), as one moves to the level of the mind, he discovers the beauty of the soul.

18.13.s.en: 6. The wicked are driven from their tents

18.13.0.en: 14 He is cut off from his tent, from his confidence, and is driven to the king of terrors. 15 One who is not his dwells in his tent. Brimstone is scattered on his dwelling.

18.13.1.en: "He is cut off from his tent, from his confidence, and is driven to the king of terrors" [14].

18.13.2.en: The man who lives in this world for the body and its lusts loses even this body, or this tent, and death comes upon him, not as a joyful passage to heaven, but as the "king of terrors."

18.13.3.en: Everything he depended on as his master is taken from him, and nothing is left to him of what he depended on, not even his tent. His soul was his confidence, but it is uprooted from the tent of the body, so the body has no support at all. This is what was said to the foolish rich man: "This night thy soul shall be required of thee" (Lk 12:20).

18.13.4.en: The text in the writings of Pope Gregory (the Great) reads: "Let his confidence be uprooted from his tent, and let death tread upon him as a king." He sees that death here is Satan, to whom the wicked man surrenders himself and submits as to a king, as it also refers to sin, which humiliates the wicked man and enslaves him.

18.13.5.en: * The title "Death" in this place refers to (the devil), the enemy of the human race himself, who brought in death. He spread by a certain servant of (the enemy), of whom it was said to John: "and his name that sat on him was Death" (Rev 6:8). So this death treads upon the wicked man as a king, on the day of his departure from here. For the one who deceived him before with gentle allurements carries him in the end to punishment in chains by violence, and brings him down harshly, binding him by force with evil works.

18.13.6.en: And here also, when death takes possession of the heart of the lost sinner, it treads upon him at the very time when it presses upon him with the feeling of pleasure. It is as though he sets on him the feet of his tyrannical authority.

18.13.7.en: But if we understand by death not the devil openly but sin, whose fruit is death on the day of judgment, then truly such a death treads upon the mind as a king, when it reigns over a person without resistance from him. For the temptation of sin cannot be far from a man who stands in this life. But resisting the temptations of sin is one thing, and being enslaved to its tyranny over us is another. So the wicked man, since he does not learn to resist the enticements of sin, and does not fear to submit to its authority, of him it is said: ["Death as a king treads upon him"]. It is the reign of this death that Paul guarded against, lest it rule over the hearts of his disciples, when he said: ["Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body"] (Rom 6:12).

18.13.9.en: * Those who live in pleasures fear death, but the sorrowful long for it that they may depart quickly.

18.13.10.en: The rich fear death, and the poor desire it that they may rest from their toils.

18.13.11.en: The strong are terrified when they remember it, and the sick look to it in hope that they may rest from their pains.

18.13.12.en: Fr. Aphrahat * He who loves earthly things and their lusts does not think of being with Christ after his departure, and cannot say: ["I am a stranger in the earth"](a), for he is concerned with the things of the earth. But he who says, "hide not thy commandments from me," is a saint... Therefore the prophet asks God to reveal to him the great things of His commandments for the heavenly life.

18.13.13.en: Origen * Surely he fears death who has not been born of water and the Spirit, for he is delivered to the fires of hell.

18.13.14.en: He fears death who has not experienced the cross of Christ and His sufferings.

18.13.15.en: He fears death who awaits another death after death.

18.13.16.en: He fears death for whom the fires of eternity and endless punishment are waiting.

18.13.17.en: He fears death who finds benefit in postponing his death so that his sighs and groans may be delayed.

18.13.18.en: St. Cyprian the Martyr "One who is not his dwells in his tent."

18.14.1.en: God created man to be the storehouse of His love and tenderness and rich grace and goodness, but if man persists in refusing to cleave to God, a curse comes upon his tent, where his body, like his soul, becomes a dwelling for the enemy of good, who usurps what is not his own. Man turns into a lair for the devil, receiving brimstone and fire like Sodom and Gomorrah, instead of being a holy temple of God.

18.14.2.en: St. Macarius sees that the inner man is either a land that God inhabits as His sanctuary, or the enemy of good occupies it and makes it his land, and it becomes satanic. By "land" he means "dwelling."

18.14.3.en: * ["Let brimstone be scattered on his dwelling"] [15]. What is brimstone but the fuel that kindles fire and sends out of it a very foul smell? What then do we understand by brimstone but fleshly sin, which, as it fills the mind with evil thoughts, like a kind of corrupt odor kindles an eternal fire for itself. And while the clouds of its smell spread in the lost soul, it is as one who supplies fuel to the flame of its destruction. By this the foul smell of the flesh is understood as brimstone.

18.14.4.en: The history of the Holy Bible itself records this, telling us that the Lord rained fire and brimstone on Sodom (Gen 19:14)... Thus "let brimstone be scattered on his dwelling."

18.15.0.en: The wicked man, by corrupting leniency toward the body that exercises authority within him, is occupied by evil thoughts without ceasing, and they prevent him from producing the fruit of good work. Therefore it was rightly said: ["His roots shall be dried up beneath, and above shall his harvest be corrupted"] [16].

18.15.2.en: * There is a land inhabited by wild beasts, and a land in the air in which birds move and live. If the birds wish to stand and walk on the ground, the hunters snare them. The fish also have a land, the waters of the sea. The place in which any creature is born, whether on the earth or in the air, in it it lives, in it it feeds, and finds its delight and rest.

18.15.3.en: In the same way there is a land of Satan and a house for him, in which the powers of darkness and the spirits of evil live. In it they move and find their rest. As there is also a land of light, the land of divinity, where the camps of angels and holy spirits ascend and descend upon it and find their rest in it.

18.15.4.en: The eyes of the body cannot see the dark land or touch it, and so also with the land of light, which is the land of divinity... But to the spiritual, the satanic land of darkness and the land of divinity are revealed to the eyes of their hearts.

18.15.5.en: St. Macarius the Great * You should know that we become bodies for them (the demons) when our souls accept their dark, evil thoughts, and when they become manifest through our body in which we dwell.

18.15.6.en: St. Abba Anthony the Great * Do not be a companion of the quarrelsome, lest a chorus of demons dwell in your house.

18.15.7.en: Beware of the one who bears a grudge, for he is a devil incarnate.

18.15.9.en: * It is clear that unclean spirits cannot find a way into the bodies of those whom they have seized by any means unless they first reign over their minds and thoughts, robbing them of the fear of God and of remembering Him and meditating on Him, and by this they dare to approach them as those who have no divine protection, and bind them easily, and find a place in them, as if they had the right of ownership over them.

18.15.10.en: Fr. Serenus Some see that Bildad heard of the fire that came down from heaven and burned Job's sheep and servants, so he supposed that Job, with all his possessions, had reached in his wickedness what Sodom and Gomorrah had reached, and deserved the fires of God's wrath to burn what Job did not deserve or what he had usurped, for he was dwelling in a house not his.

18.15.11.en: * (The godly man) the beauty of his virtues is not changed by a savage death. The health that is brought to him by his prayers is not removed from his tent (his body), as long as he is indeed rich in practicing good works, and if his wealth is lost he remains radiant with the splendor of righteousness through his patience...

18.15.12.en: ["His loftiness is scattered with brimstone."] This is what truly happened to the sinners in Sodom and Gomorrah, for what happened partially to the wicked (in Sodom and Gomorrah) the other wicked expect to happen to them in this present world or the world to come.

18.16.s.en: 7. The remembrance of the wicked removed

18.16.0.en: 16 His roots shall be dried up beneath, and above shall his branch be cut off. 17 His remembrance shall perish from the earth, and he shall have no name on the face of the land.

18.16.1.en: "His roots shall be dried up beneath, and above shall his branch be cut off" [16].

18.16.2.en: When man, by his persistence in evil, loses the riches of God's surpassing grace, he becomes like one stripped of his roots, that is, of his blessed fathers, and is like a tree whose roots are dried up, with no life left in it. He also loses his offspring, like a tree whose branches are dried up, so that there is no fruit in it. This is what many wicked men fell into, such as Jeroboam, Baasha and Ahab, and not one of their offspring was left alive.

18.16.3.en: If our roots have dried up, the Lord Christ has offered Himself as a root overflowing within us with His divine life, and our branches are refreshed to bear the fruit of His Holy Spirit: love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance (Gal 5:22-23).

18.16.4.en: The text in the writings of Pope Gregory (the Great) reads: "Let his roots dry up beneath, and let his harvest be corrupted above."

18.16.5.en: * What do we understand by the title "his roots," hidden from sight, which put forth a branch that is seen openly, but the unseen thoughts in the heart, which produce visible works? So also by the title "harvest" he refers to that visible practice which comes from the hidden root... The wicked man puts his thoughts on lower things, and ignores seeking the delights of eternal greenness, and what is this but that he leaves [his roots to dry up beneath]? ["Let his harvest be corrupted above"], since his patience is counted as nothing in the eyes of heaven, even if it is counted good in the eyes of man. Thus the roots are beneath, and the harvest above, in that we first send good thoughts here, so that we may one day be made worthy to receive the fruit of our good works in an eternal reward.

18.17.0.en: "His remembrance shall perish from the earth, and he shall have no name on the face of the land" [17].

18.17.1.en: Nothing occupies the mind of the devil like vainglory; because of it he rebelled against God and fell. And because of it he fights the children of men, supposing that he reigns over their hearts and thoughts, and that his reign over them will last forever.

18.17.2.en: His children imitate him, so they seek temporal glory, and think that the world will immortalize their names, offering every human work that will establish their memory through history. But evil blots out their name from the book of life. And when the name of the wicked man is removed from the book of life in heaven, his honor is buried in the dust, and his name bears nothing but contempt and disdain even on earth, "he shall have no name on the face of the land." He receives here a foretaste of the eternal shame and disgrace that he will face on the great day of the Lord. "The memory of the just is blessed: but the name of the wicked shall rot" (Prov 10:7).

18.17.3.en: It was said of the wicked:

18.17.4.en: "O thou enemy, destructions are come to a perpetual end: and thou hast destroyed cities; their memorial is perished with them" (Ps 9:6).

18.17.5.en: "When he maketh inquisition for blood, he remembereth them: he forgetteth not the cry of the humble" (Ps 9:12).

18.17.6.en: "The face of the LORD is against them that do evil, to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth" (Ps 34:16).

18.17.7.en: "Let them be before the LORD continually, that he may cut off the memory of them from the earth" (Ps 109:15).

18.17.8.en: "For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know not any thing, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten" (Eccl 9:5).

18.17.9.en: ["They shall fall hereafter a shameful fall, and be a reproach among the dead for evermore: for he will dash them speechless, with heads bowed down, and shake them from the foundations; and they shall be utterly laid waste, and be in sorrow; and their memorial shall perish"] (Wis 4:19).

18.17.10.en: "He dried up some of them and destroyed their inhabitants, and removed their memory from the earth" (Sir 10:20).

18.17.11.en: And it was said of the righteous:

18.17.12.en: "His memorial shall not depart away, and his name shall live from generation to generation" (Sir 39:13).

18.17.13.en: "Let their memorial be blessed, and let their bones flourish again out of their place" (Sir 46:14).

18.17.14.en: "And Nehemias, whose memorial is for all days, who raised up for us the walls that were fallen, and set up the gates and the bars, and raised up our ruined houses again" (Sir 49:15).

18.17.15.en: * "Let his memory be removed from the earth, and let his name not be found in public places" (LXX). It is clear that this concerns those who must dwell in this darkness, those whom Christ appointed [to be in outer darkness (Mt 8:12; 25:30)], those who take part in the wedding feast in filthy garments, and the king says: Bind his hands and feet... and cast him into outer darkness, where there is weeping and gnashing of teeth, for many are called but few are chosen (see Mt 22:13-14).

18.17.16.en: ["And their name is not found"], because the wicked are driven out of the land of the righteous, and are taken to be with those whose names are blotted out forever (Deut 32:26). Therefore David sang elsewhere on the harp: "Thou hast put out their name for ever and ever" (Ps 9:5).

18.17.17.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * ["His memory perishes from the earth, and his name is not heard in the streets."] It is fitting to notice that Bildad the Shuhite expressed himself about each one of the wicked, so that his words are secretly directed against the chief of all the wicked. For the chief of the wicked is Satan. He himself enters in the last times into this vessel of destruction, who is called the "antichrist," and who seeks to spread his name everywhere. Every person, even now, likens himself to the antichrist when he strives to spread the memory of his earthly name through the glory of praise and by exalting himself with temporal fame. Therefore may every wicked person understand these words, and may they also point especially to the chief of the wicked himself.

18.18.0.en: 18 He is driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the world. 19 He has neither son nor descendant among his people, nor any survivor in his dwellings. 20 They that come after him shall be astonied at his day, and they of old shudder. 21 Surely such are the dwellings of the wicked, and this is the place of him that knoweth not God.

18.18.1.en: "He is driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the world" [18].

18.18.2.en: The wicked man is driven from what he thinks is light in this world, because of the comfort he obtained, into the darkness of the grave, and from it into outer darkness, where "they shall never see light" (Ps 49:19), and have no hope at all.

18.18.3.en: The wicked man is chased out of the world, that is, out of the pleasures of the world which he thought inhabited, and he goes out as with his first parents Adam and Eve from Paradise. So he is driven from the chamber of the heavenly Bridegroom, where there is no place for him, and remains in outer darkness eternally.

18.18.4.en: * "Thou hast put out their name for ever and ever" (Ps 9:5). You destroy them utterly, uproot them from their roots, and blot them out so that their memory also disappears... "Their memorial is perished with a crashing" and in another text "their memorial is perished with them." What does he mean by saying "with a crashing"? He speaks of total destruction, or of the hideousness of the evils. And this in fact is a sign of God's providence, that He does not do this in secret, so that He may reform men through the misfortunes of others. Therefore he points to the fame of the destruction that comes upon them.

18.18.5.en: St. John Chrysostom * "The eyes of the LORD are upon the righteous, and his ears are open unto their cry" (Ps 34:15)... Perhaps you will say: I have cried to Him, yet I am still in distress. Only hold fast to His ways, and when you are in distress He hears you.

18.18.6.en: He is a physician, and gives you a kind of cleansing. You cry out, but He keeps cutting and does not lift His hand until He has cut as He pleases. For a physician who listens to the person and stops wounding and cleansing is cruel.

18.18.7.en: Mothers keep on bathing their children for their health. Do the children not cry in their hands? Are these mothers cruel because they do not stop and do not care about their children's tears? Are they not full of tenderness...? So God also is full of love, but He seems like one who does not hear. For He does not stop until He heals us eternally.

18.18.8.en: Perhaps the wicked man will say: I do evil and I am safe, for the eyes of the Lord are not upon me, but the Lord listens to the righteous, and not to me; I do what I want and I am safe. Since the Lord sees the thoughts of men, it was said: "The face of the LORD is against them that do evil, to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth" (Ps 34:16).

18.18.9.en: St. Augustine * ["He drives him from light into darkness"] [18]. Man is driven from light into darkness when he falls under eternal judgment because of the love of receiving the honor of the present life.

18.18.11.en: Bildad and his friends thought that Job's name would perish from the earth, because he was wicked. So also the Jews wished to destroy the name of Jesus by crucifying Him, so that in its place the name of the robber Barabbas might arise. But their name perished and the name of Jesus remained glorified, and will be glorified forever. And what was directed against Job and against the Lord Christ the world continues to direct against the Church, that her name may be destroyed from the earth, bringing continual accusations against her. But the Church remains the holy Bride, her life bearing witness to the surpassing riches of God's grace, and enjoying fellowship of glory eternally.

18.19.0.en: "He has neither son nor descendant (heel) among his people, nor any survivor in his dwellings (nor any remaining in his habitations)" [19].

18.19.1.en: The spiritual man is a living witness to the Gospel of Christ, and gains many as offspring for himself in the Lord. The Apostle John calls those he serves "my little children." And the Apostle Paul speaks of his disciple Onesimus, saying: "whom I have begotten in my bonds" (Phlm 10). But the wicked man, even if he has many children according to the flesh, has no son or grandson who enjoys any wealth and bears his name and memory.

18.19.2.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that this saying does not apply to the righteous Job, but to the wicked devil, as it applies to the antichrist who thinks he rules the whole world.

18.19.3.en: This saying applies to all the wicked, especially Judas, who betrayed his Lord because of his love of silver, for it was said of him: "For it is written in the book of Psalms, Let his habitation be desolate, and let no man dwell therein: and his bishoprick let another take" (Acts 1:20).

18.19.4.en: "O thou enemy, destructions are come to a perpetual end" (Ps 9:6).

18.19.5.en: "Let their habitation be desolate; and let none dwell in their tents" (Ps 69:25).

18.19.6.en: * ["He has neither son nor descendant among his people, nor any remnant in his sides"] [19]. For it is written that the Lord Jesus "shall consume with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming" (2 Thess 2:8). And so, since his evil ends at the same time as the end of the world, [he has no offspring among his people], for he and his people together are driven on the same level to punishment. All the wicked who walked in evil by his evil counsel are struck by the brightness of the Lord's coming with eternal ruin, together with this their chief (Satan). He has no offspring remaining in the world, for the just Judge ends his evils at one time with the end of the world. Now these words are understood as specifically about the antichrist, since there was added to them: ["They that come after him shall be astonied at his day, and they of old shudder"] [20].

18.19.8.en: * "But strangers dwell in his place" [19 LXX]. The blessings of the age to come have been prepared wholly for all, if they will walk in the way of God (Ps 25:10). Places there have been prepared for all (Jn 14:2-3), if they will be watchful. But those who do not walk in the way of God can open themselves so that they (demons or sins) may enter into them. Therefore he said: ["Strangers also live in his place"], meaning that those who walk in the way of God live far from the wicked (the evil spirits).

18.20.0.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem "They that come after him shall be astonied at his day, and they of old shudder" [20].

18.20.1.en: When the curse comes upon the wicked man and he falls into a sudden bitter change that no one expected, and of which neither those before him nor those after him had heard, they cry out in amazement: ["How terrible are Thy judgments, O Lord!"] (see Ps 66:3).

18.20.2.en: The element of surprise at what will befall the wicked, especially on the day of judgment, amazes the righteous who preceded him, and also his contemporaries. For however the distress that comes upon them is described, it cannot express what they will suffer. And in the same way with the righteous, for no human mind can imagine the glory prepared for them.

18.20.3.en: Perhaps, while speaking here of the wicked, he is speaking of the most dangerous of them, the antichrist, who appears as a king with authority, to whom many peoples submit, and who controls the outlets of the world, but he suddenly collapses when God sends help to His Church, and destruction comes upon the antichrist.

18.20.4.en: * ["They that come after him shall be astonied at his day, and they of old shudder"] [20]. For he (Satan) will be loosed to stand against the righteous with such evil, that the hearts of the chosen will be struck with no little terror. It is written: "insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect" (Mt 24:24). This was said clearly not because the chosen will fall, but because they will be terrified by fearful dangers.

18.20.6.en: * ["Those who come later groan deeply over him, and astonishment seizes those of old"] [20]. Bildad calls those who are made worthy to receive the wages at the eleventh hour (Mt 20:9), through repentance, the latecomers. Rightly they sigh over the wicked, asking themselves why these also did not desire to obtain spiritual prosperity through profitable repentance.

18.20.7.en: ["And astonishment seizes those of old"], those who from the beginning fulfilled the commandments of God... meaning how even at the end of time these (the wicked) did not submit to God's commandment.

18.21.0.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem "Surely such are the dwellings of the wicked, and this is the place of him that knoweth not God" [21].

18.21.1.en: This is what comes upon the dwellings of the wicked of desolation and ruin, misery and wretchedness. ["Those who know not God await vengeance"] (2 Thess 1:8). What is the dwelling of the wicked who persisted in not knowing God but eternal hell.

18.21.2.en: St. Hippolytus says in his treatise Against Plato, on the Cause of the Universe, if this work is authentic, that souls after death are led by a guardian angel to Hades, to a wide and dark place, where they remain until the day of resurrection, some of them wicked souls deserving temporary punishment for their wickedness, as a foretaste of the eternal punishment that awaits them. They remain beside the lake of fire which is hell, see its flame, smell its smoke, and are filled with terror because of the coming judgment, but the righteous are led to a place more radiant, and more joyful than the lower world, called "Abraham's bosom," where they enjoy fellowship with the angels and the patriarchs (the Fathers), and rejoice at seeing the reward to come.

18.21.3.en: St. John Chrysostom did not wish to speak of the location of hell other than that it is "outside this world." But he spoke in some detail of its torments. In one of his homilies he says of it:

18.21.4.en: [It is a sea of fire, not a sea of the same kind and dimensions as we know here, but greater and fiercer, with waves of fire, strange, terrifying fires. There is a great abyss there filled with terrifying flame. One can see fire coming out of it on every side like a ravening beast...

18.21.5.en: There none can resist, none can escape.

18.21.6.en: There the gentle face of Christ, the giver of peace, is seen nowhere.

18.21.7.en: And as those condemned to work in the mines are violent men, who no longer see their families but those who put them to forced labor, so it will be there, but not so simply, but far worse. For here a man can present a petition to the emperor asking for mercy, and the prisoner may be pardoned, but there this will not happen. They will not go out but remain, enduring torments that cannot be expressed.]

18.21.8.en: Again he says that the fires there do not consume the person, and give no light, but burn continually. For the resurrected bodies of the condemned are changed to incorruption, therefore they remain suffering torments eternally.

18.21.9.en: St. John Chrysostom sees that the degrees of torment in hell differ, depending on the extent of man's sins, but all fall under it eternally. He also says that God prepares hell so that no one may be cast into it(b).

18.21.10.en: * It is impossible that the torments of hell do not exist.

18.21.11.en: * These torments are not merely for the fulfillment of divine justice, but were established to urge mankind to repent and abstain from sin.

18.21.12.en: * If God is concerned that we not sin, and that we enter into troubles such as these for our correction, it is clear that He punishes sinners and crowns the righteous.

18.21.13.en: St. John Chrysostom * I wonder how man makes light of the fire on the day of judgment. They fear the flame of the furnace, and do not care about the fire of hell, as though it were nothing. Why are they so insensible and heedless of the matter? Why are their hearts so perverse?

18.21.14.en: St. Augustine * ["Is this also the place of those who know not the Lord?"] [21 LXX]. Who are those who did not accept this (place)? And how? The Only-Begotten Son declares this (place) to us plainly: "Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels: for I was an hungred, and ye gave me no meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me no drink" (Mt 25:41-42)... But you do not doubt that Bildad was able to understand this or utter it, for the natural law proclaims the judgment of God. All men, when they receive the natural law in their lives in a sound way, know what awaits the righteous and what awaits sinners. And also those who disobey cannot make excuse before the great and awesome Judge. But Bildad deserves blame and contempt all the more, because, while knowing what belongs to the wicked, he basely confused them with Job. In this he is like those who call fornicators chaste, the covetous righteous, and hypocrites humble...

18.21.15.en: As for us, let us distinguish the good from the wicked, and as we praise the righteous let us sanctify our words and cleanse our hearts. And at the same time let us consecrate our bodies and our souls and the temples of our souls with our zeal, together with our esteem for the righteous and our glorifying of God, who is pleased with the honor of His servants. To Him be glory forever and ever. Amen.

18.21.16.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * The gnashing of teeth (as the Lord described it in eternal hell) is not a gnashing of bodily teeth, nor is the worm a bodily one. These things were written only because the worm appears with severe fever (sickness), and so he who does not repent and is not cleansed of his sins will burn in his fire and be eaten by his worm (his works). Therefore Isaiah wrote: Walk in your fires, and in the sparks that ye have kindled (Isa 50:11). They are the fires of the dejection of sin and its result. It is like a worm, because the sins of the soul pierce the mind and heart, and eat the bowels of the conscience.

18.21.17.en: St. Ambrose * ["Surely such are the dwellings of the wicked, and this is the place of him that knoweth not God"] [21]. For he had said before: ["He drives him from light into darkness, and chases him out of the world"] [18]. And to his miseries there follows: ["Surely such are the dwellings of the wicked, and this is the place of him that knoweth not God."] He who now boasts of not knowing God is driven to his dwelling, when his wickedness thrusts him into woes, and he finds himself one day in the darkness of his place, while he made himself happy here in the false light of the righteous, and so occupied another's place. For the wicked in all that they do with deceit strive to gain for themselves the title "righteous," as those who occupy another's place. But then they are brought to their own place when they are tormented with eternal fire as the fruit of their iniquity.

18.21.19.en: You are my life, and without You I have no life

18.21.20.en: * My God, You are the eternal Light, You enlighten my depths, and turn me into a light for the world; without You my lamp goes out, and my house turns into a tomb.

18.21.21.en: And I lose all warmth and life!

18.21.22.en: * Lead my soul, for You are the Way.

18.21.23.en: Without You I stumble in the darkness, I fall and do not rise.

18.21.24.en: By You I set out to heaven, and walk the journey of my life in safety!

18.21.25.en: * You are the Truth, in You I set out to true knowledge.

18.21.26.en: Without You I become like a straying beast.

18.21.27.en: Or like an animal without awareness.

18.21.28.en: I fall into the snares of the devil, and become a laughingstock to him!

18.21.29.en: Rescue me from the snares of the enemy, and I will be like a bird that escapes from a broken snare, flying in complete freedom!

18.21.32.en: It devours me, and there is no deliverer!

18.21.33.en: I live as in an unbearable hell.

18.21.34.en: Come, O Life, and fill my depths with Your peace!

18.21.35.en: * You are my treasure and my wealth.

18.21.36.en: I possess You, and so everything is in my hands.

18.21.37.en: I will not feel want, and no trial will be able to crush me.

18.21.39.en: You counted me a son to You!

18.21.40.en: I draw near to You, and I find You in my depths, not far from me.

18.21.41.en: Who can separate me from You?

18.21.42.en: Finally, grant me to possess You, O Holy One, and evil will flee from me, and the enemy will find no place in me.

18.21.43.en: Rather, let me taste the earnest of Your heavens!

18.21.44.en: * My God, You are my all!

18.21.45.en: You are my light, dispelling the darkness.

18.21.47.en: You are the Truth that cannot be resisted!

18.21.48.en: You are the mystery of my salvation.

18.21.49.en: You are my treasure that cannot be stolen, and my wealth that cannot be taken from me.

18.21.50.en: You are my heavenly Father, You embrace me in Your arms!
